title: Staff economic projections
summary: This page documents the Bank of Canada's Staff Economic Projections database, describing its structure, variables tracked (GDP, CPI, unemployment, exchange rates, policy rates), data formats (CSV/JSON/XML via Valet API), and release policies. Data is released with a five-year lag; most recent vintage available is 2019Q4.
key_points: Staff economic projections are provided to Governing Council before monetary policy decisions and released publicly with a five-year lag.
Most recent vintage available is 2019Q4, meaning the data is over six years old as of April 2026.
Variables tracked include Real GDP, CPI, Core CPI, unemployment rate, U.S./CAD exchange rate, and staff projection policy rate.
The staff projection policy rate may differ from Governing Council's actual policy rate.
Data available in CSV, JSON, and XML formats via the Bank of Canada's Valet API.
Historical data vintages span from approximately 1970s through 2019Q4.
why_it_matters: This documentation page describes how to access Bank of Canada historical staff forecasts for research purposes. The five-year release lag and 2019Q4 vintage limit relevance to current macro analysis but may be useful for historical research on forecast methodology and monetary policy credibility.
macro_context: This is database documentation with no current macro relevance. The 2019Q4 vintage predates the COVID-19 pandemic, 2020-2022 inflation surge, and subsequent Bank of Canada rate cycles.
market_structure_context: The Valet API provides machine-readable access to historical forecast vintages, which could be useful for backtesting or studying central bank forecast accuracy.
